short_answer: Mike Barner is a real and active writer. RotoWire says he has covered fantasy sports since 2007 and joined RotoWire in 2010, and PrizePicks and RotoWire both list articles by him from November 2026. On SportsLine he is billed as an NBA Guru and posts NBA player prop picks almost every day; his page showed picks for 12 to 18 Nov 2026. We found no link to WagerTalk on any page we opened.

You cannot buy Barner alone. His picks sit behind SportsLine Pro, which cost $13.99 a month, $39.99 for three months or $139.99 a year on 19 Nov 2026 and also unlocks every other SportsLine expert. SportsLine's terms say cancelling stops the renewal but you will not get a refund of fees paid.

SportsLine and CBS Sports articles describe him as a strong prop bettor: 407-314 over two NBA seasons, returning $3,628 to $100 bettors. Taking the numbers on SportsLine's own pages at face value, almost all of that profit came in 2024/25. The newest stretch we could see was weaker: his last 15 listed picks went 7-8, about 1.75 units down by our count, and a forum member's running tally had him 37-42 between 18 Apr and 5 Jun 2026. We found no buyer reviews of him anywhere.

guarantee: There is no win guarantee of any kind. SportsLine's subscription terms describe "a subscription fee, that will automatically renew and be charged to your Payment Method at the then current rate" unless you cancel.

If you cancel, the terms say "YOU WILL NOT RECEIVE A REFUND OF ANY FEES PAID" and that "cancellation of your subscription is your sole recourse if you have any dissatisfaction." The terms list cancellation by phone at 1 888 508 3055 or by email to support@sportsline.com.
Nothing covers the money you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: SportsLine and CBS Sports quote Barner's record over windows that change from article to article: two seasons, one season, a 161 pick run, a 225 pick run. A CBS Sports article adds that anyone following "could have seen huge returns." None of the pages we opened give the full list behind those windows, so you cannot check how each window was chosen.

All 15 picks we saw were overs on player stats, priced from -101 to -132, about -115 on average. At that average price he needs to win about 53.4% just to break even, more than the 52.4% needed at -110.
record: What we checked ourselves: the SportsLine page listed 15 picks for games from 12 to 18 Nov 2026, each 1 unit, each with the time it was posted, the odds and the sportsbook. We counted 7 wins and 8 losses. Wins at the listed odds add about 6.25 units, losses cost 8, so the stretch is about 1.75 units down. Fifteen picks prove nothing either way, but they are the most recent evidence.

Using only SportsLine's own figures: 407-314 over two seasons returning $3,628, and 239-178-2 returning $3,209 for 2024/25. The difference is 168-136 (55.3%) and $419 for the other season, assuming the two season figure is 2024/25 plus 2025/26. That is a winning record but a thin margin on mostly juiced overs.

Independent tracking: a TheRX member who reposts Barner's SportsLine picks adds a running record in brackets. It read 84-43 on 26 Mar 2026, 90-49 on 1 Apr, 101-62 on 18 Apr and 138-104 on 5 Jun 2026. These line up closely with the runs SportsLine advertised, so they likely copy the same counter rather than grade picks separately. Between 18 Apr and 5 Jun the tally went 37-42 (46.8%). We did not grade those picks ourselves.
SportsLine is both the store and the scorekeeper for these numbers.

our_data.text: In this edition no Mike Barner pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Mike Barner performs.

customers_intro: We looked for buyer reviews on Reddit (through an archive), TheRX, Sportsbook Review, Covers and our own library. What exists is a set of TheRX forum posts that copy his paid SportsLine picks with a running record. We found no post from anyone describing what it was like to buy or follow him.

customers.text: We found about half a dozen TheRX forum posts from March to June 2026, plus one from 2022, that repost Barner's SportsLine prop picks, usually with a running record in brackets. Nobody replied to them with an opinion; each drew a couple of likes. The running record climbed from 84-43 in late March to 101-62 in mid April, then cooled to 138-104 by early June, a 37-42 stretch. Our Reddit post search found only posts about a football player with the same surname (comment search timed out), and our library held only social accounts that repost his picks. We found no buyer review, positive or negative, on any site we checked.
A TheRX member posted a Barner NBA prop pick with the record line 3-4 (84~43), meaning a 3-4 recent stretch inside a larger 84-43 run.
The same kind of post listed two Barner overs with the record line 3-2 (90~49).
A TheRX post listed four Barner plays with the record NBA 3-3 (101-62). CBS Sports quoted his run as 101-60 the same day.
A TheRX post listed a Barner points over with no record. The thread's own rules list SportsLine among services members are asked not to post, yet his plays kept appearing.
A TheRX post listed three Barner overs with the record line 0-2 / 138~104. Compared with the 18 Apr post, that is 37 wins and 42 losses in between, during the NBA playoffs.
An older TheRX post included a Barner side pick in a list of many services, showing his SportsLine plays were being shared on forums by 2022.

We found no buyer review of Mike Barner on Sportsbook Review, Covers, the App Store or the Better Business Bureau. On Reddit, post titles and text naming Barner were all about a football player with the same surname; the archive's comment search timed out, so our Reddit check was partial. Reviews of SportsLine as a whole exist and are covered on our SportsLine page; they rarely name individual experts.

conflicts: SportsLine sells Barner's picks, grades them and writes the articles that advertise his runs. CBS Sports, which publishes those articles, belongs to the same company.

Barner also writes betting and fantasy content for RotoWire and PrizePicks, a daily fantasy pick'em operator. Writing for an operator is common in this industry, but it means part of his income can come from the betting side, not only from subscribers.
strengths: A real, named writer with a long public history: fantasy sports since 2007, RotoWire since 2010, and writing award finalist recognition confirmed on more than one site.
SportsLine lists each pick with the time it was posted, the odds, the sportsbook and the result, losses included.
Cheap entry compared with most pick sellers: $13.99 for a month, and that buys every SportsLine expert, not just Barner.
Even by SportsLine's own numbers his edge is modest rather than miraculous, and his advertised records are above the break even line rather than claims of 70% or more.
concerns: No refunds and no guarantee; the subscription renews automatically until you cancel.
Records are quoted over windows that change between articles, and the full history behind them is not shown on the pages we read.
By SportsLine's own figures, his second season returned only about $419 to $100 bettors after a $3,209 season before it.
Recent form is cooler: 7-8 on the last 15 listed picks and 37-42 on a forum tally from 18 Apr to 5 Jun 2026, on overs that are often priced at -115 or worse.
checklist: Open his SportsLine page before paying and count the last 50 to 100 picks yourself, at the listed odds.
Count units, not wins. Overs at -120 and -125 need well over 52.4% to make money.
Check whether you can still get his number. Prop lines move fast after a pick is posted.
Set a reminder to cancel. SportsLine renews automatically and the terms say no refund of fees paid.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long time fantasy and betting writer whose picks are sold through SportsLine, a CBS owned subscription. That makes him a legitimate seller. Whether his picks win over time is not proven: the records come from SportsLine itself, and his most recent visible stretch was 7-8.
How much do Mike Barner's picks cost?
You cannot buy him alone. On 19 Nov 2026 SportsLine Pro cost $13.99 a month, $39.99 for three months or $139.99 a year, and that covers every SportsLine expert.
Does Mike Barner have a verified record?

No independent one. SportsLine claims 407-314 on NBA props over two seasons. A TheRX member's running tally, which seems to copy SportsLine's own counter, went from 101-62 on 18 Apr to 138-104 on 5 Jun 2026.
Does Mike Barner sell picks on WagerTalk?
We found no Mike Barner page on WagerTalk and no mention of WagerTalk in his bios. The pages we opened tie his paid picks to SportsLine, and his articles to RotoWire and PrizePicks.
Can I get a refund from SportsLine?
No. SportsLine's terms say that if you cancel you will not receive a refund of any fees paid, and that cancelling is your sole recourse if you are unhappy.

At $13.99 a month for all SportsLine experts the entry cost is low. But his picks are mostly juiced overs, his edge by SportsLine's own numbers shrank sharply in the second of his two advertised seasons, and we found no buyer reviews either way. Track his listed picks for a while before you bet real money on them.
